composition.story: Recursive feature elimination drops the weakest feature, then refits. Features x1 and x2 share one signal, so each looks weak alone. Step through four features down to one. Watch x2's weight after x1 leaves, then compare with fitting once.

aha.observation: After x1 is dropped, the refit gives x2 weight 0.59, up from 0.31. Old weights were stale, so refitting prevents dropping x2 by mistake.

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous / Next buttons over the step rail; keyboard arrows move one state

controls.label: Elimination method
controls.presentation: Select switching between the two variants; each restarts at its first state

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Returns to the first state and Refit each round

regions.label: Linear model fit on remaining features

states.label: Start
states.sentence: Four features are in. x1 and x2 carry nearly the same signal. The goal is to keep one feature.
states.why: Shared signal means weights depend on which features are present.

states.label: Fit 1
states.sentence: Fit 1 on all four: x1 0.30, x2 0.31, x3 0.40, x4 0.05. The twins split their shared weight.
states.why: Each twin gets about half of the signal they share.

states.label: Drop x4
states.sentence: x4 has the smallest weight, so x4 is dropped. This choice is safe because x4 is noise.
states.why: The lowest weight is removed first.

states.label: Fit 2
states.sentence: Refit on x1, x2, x3: weights barely move, because x4 shared no signal with them.
states.why: Refitting changes little when the dropped feature was independent.

states.label: Drop x1
states.sentence: x1 is now lowest, so x1 is dropped. Its shared signal has to go somewhere.
states.why: Removing one twin leaves its signal for the other twin to carry.

states.label: Fit 3: refit
states.sentence: Refit on x2, x3: x2 jumps from 0.31 to 0.59. It absorbed x1's share.
states.why: The old 0.31 was stale. Weights are w(S), valid only for the current feature set S.

states.label: Drop x3
states.sentence: Now x3 is lowest, so x3 is dropped. x2 remains as the best single feature.
states.why: Fresh weights rank x2 above x3, the reverse of the stale ranking.

regions.label: Linear model fit once on all features

states.label: Start
states.sentence: Same four features, but the model is fit only once. The goal is still to keep one feature.
states.why: Every later drop will reuse the first fit's weights.

states.label: Single fit
states.sentence: The one fit gives x1 0.30, x2 0.31, x3 0.40, x4 0.05. This ranking is never updated.
states.why: The ranking is fixed from now on.

states.label: Drop x4
states.sentence: x4 is lowest and is dropped. This matches the refit run so far.
states.why: Dropping noise is correct either way.

states.label: Drop x1
states.sentence: x1 is next lowest on the old ranking and is dropped. Nothing checks how x2 changed.
states.why: The old ranking cannot see x2 absorbing x1's signal.

states.label: Drop x2 (wrong)
states.sentence: Stale x2 at 0.31 is below x3 at 0.40, so x2 is dropped. x3 is kept, which is wrong.
states.why: The true x2 weight is 0.59, but without a refit it is never measured.

1.reason: The scene asks whether a twin's weight changes after its partner is dropped; the x1/x2 shared-signal link and the fit3 weights (x2 0.31→0.59) demonstrate it.

2.reason: The aha state fit3 is a stepper state that holds until the learner presses Next, with the decisive x2 jump shown in the callout and readout.

3.reason: The method select changes the outcome: refit keeps x2, fit once drops x2 on stale weights and wrongly keeps x3.

4.reason: The callout targets, active highlights, ghost (previous.active), links and readouts all trace to declared regions and state fields.

6.reason: The story, the state sentences, the step labels and the mode names all refer to the same features, fits and drops in the same order.

7.reason: The refit vs fit-once comparison adds mechanism at the detailed level, with a few readouts and one callout per state and no excess marks.
